ἰξοβόρος.definition: eating mistletoe-berries, missel-thrush, Turdus viscivorus, Arist.HA617a18; cf

ἰξοεργός.definition: one who uses birdlime, fowler, AP9.264.5 , 273 tit

ἰξόομαι.definition: Pass., to be smeared with birdlime, Thphr.Ign.61

ἰξοποιέω.definition: make viscous like birdlime, of a plaster, Paul.Aeg.2.43

ἰξοφόρος.definition: having mistletoe growing thereon; limed, Opp.H.1.32

ἰοχέαιρα.definition: arrow-pourer, shooter of arrows; poison-shedding, of serpents, Nic.Fr. 33. as in yet in Pi.l.c.]

ἴπνιος.definition: of an oven:—hence; of a dunghill, Call.Fr.216

ἱππάζομαι.definition: Dor. fut. 3sg. Dialex.6.4:—drive; Pass., of the horse, to be ridden or driven, Pl.Ion540e; to be broken in for riding, X.Eq.3.1

ἱππαΐς.definition: hyperdor. for fem. of 1.3, of a knight, i.e. fibula which fastened the trabea of a Roman eques, Epigr.Gr.985.1

ἱππάκη.definition: mare's-milk cheese, used by the; horse's rennet, Dsc.2.75

ἱππέλαφος.definition: lit., horse-deer, perh. nylghau, Portax picta, Arist.HA498b32; ib.499b2

ἵππερος.definition: horse-fever, formed after etc., with a pun on , Ar.Nu.74

ἱππεύς.definition: horseman, rider, cavalryman, Sapph.Supp.5.1, cf. Hdt.3.88,9.49, A.Pers.14 , Arist.Pol.1270a29, etc.; a public courier, Aristaenet.1.26

ἱπποθήλης.definition: ass which has been suckled by a mare, such being kept for the stud, acc. to Arist.HA577b17

ἱπποθόρος.definition: covering mares, esp. of a he-; as Adj., a tune played to a mare, while she was being covered, Plu.2.138b, 704f

ἱππόομαι.definition: Pass., have the concept or idea of a horse, opp. its real existence, Plu.2.1120d, 1121a; cf

ἱππωνία.definition: Ion. buying of horses; tax on sale of horses, SIG4

ἴπωσις.definition: pressing hard, squeezing, esp. in reducing dislocations, Hp.Art.47, Heliod. ap. Orib.49.27.5 and 32.7

ἰπωτήριον.definition: olive- or wine-press, Gloss; in surgery, bougie, Heliod. ap. Orib.50.9.7, Antyll. ap. eund.44.23.61, Meges ap.eund.44.24.9

ἰπωτρίς.definition: for pressing in dislocated joints, Heliod. ap. Orib.49.32.4 and 17.9

ἰσάζω.definition: —Pass., fut. Arist.EE1243b31: aor. 1; intr. in Act., to be equal, Pl.Lg.773a, Arist.EN1154b24; Id.Pol.1304a39

ἰσαῖος.definition: late poet. form of , equality, Call.Jov.63, cf. Philostr.Jun.Im.3; an equal share, SIG57.10

ἰσάριθμος.definition: equal in number with; Gramm., of the same grammatical number, A.D.Synt.170.13. Adv. ib.143.9

ἴσκω.definition: iterat. pres. of go, Schwyzer180; = , only 3sg. impf. in

ἰσόγραφος.definition: or writing like: metaph., musical as the cicada, of Plato, Timo30.2

ἰσόζυγος.definition: Gramm., of the same number and person

ἰσοθεόω.definition: make equal to the gods, in Pass., Aesop.160

ἰσόκνημος.definition: with the legs on a level, Erot

ἰσοκρατία.definition: equality of strength or power; = equality of rights, republic, opp

ἰσόκωλος.definition: of equal members or clauses; formed of an equal number of strands, Nicom.Harm.6

ἰσοπληγής.definition: struck in the same way, Porph.in Harm.p.296W

ἰσοσκελής.definition: with equal legs, esp. in Geom., having; of numbers, that can be divided into two equal parts, even , opp. odd , Pl.Euthphr.12d

ἰσοτονία.definition: in Music, uniformity of pitch, level pitch, Ptol.Harm.1.4 , Porph.in Harm.p.287 W

ἰσοφαρίζω.definition: = match oneself with, vie; trans., make equal, Nic.Th.572

ἰσοφυής.definition: of equal growth, i.e. symmetrical; like in character, Thphr.HP3.7.4

ἰσόχρονος.definition: equal in period of revolution; contemporary, Gloss.; Vit. Theoc

ἰσόω.definition: exc. in Od. l.c.], make equal, S.El.686, Ar.V.565 , Hp.Morb.4.39:—Med., they made their nails and hands alike, i.e. used them in like manner, Hes.Sc.263:—Pass. , to be made like or equal to, Od.7.212; . . S.OT31, cf. …

ἵστημι.definition: causal, make to stand, imper. Il.21.313, E.Supp.1230, Il.9.202: impf. Ep. Od.19.574; 3pl. B.10.112: fut. Dor. Theoc.5.54: aor. 1 Ep. 3pl. for dub. in Od.18.307, 3.182, 8.435, al. : hence, in late Poets, AP9.714,708 : …

ἰσχανάω.definition: Ep. lengthd. form of : Ion; intr., c. gen., cling to, and so, long after, desire eagerly, Il.23.300; Od.8.288: c. inf., . . Il.17.572; Procl.h.Ven.2.6

ἰσχάνω.definition: Ep. lengthd. form of; get, obtain, have, had an experience . . , Epicur.Nat.27 G., cf. 51 G.; . . Vett.Val.65.13; Phld.Herc.873.6; A.R.1.902

ἰσχιάζω.definition: move the hips, of a rider, Procop.Goth.4.31; Pass., of a bandage, prob. f.l. for Gal.18.786

ἰσχνόω.definition: = make dry, Arist.Pr.885a19; put on low diet, Orib.Syn.9.37.4

ἴσχυσις.definition: mistranslation of Hebr., LXXCa.2.7, 3.5 prob. for diff. root; prob. f.l. for in Ph.1.354

ἴσχω.definition: redupl. form of (only found in pres., and; abs., hold, stay, stop! A.Ch.1052, S.Ichn.95; of ships, put in, v.l. in Th.2.91; Id.7.35, cf. A.R.2.390; of rivers, stop, Arr.An.5. 9.4:—in this sense Hom. uses Med. or Pass.…

ἴττω.definition: Boeot. for 3sg. imper. of esp. in phrase Zeus be witness! says Cebes the Theban in Pl.Phd.62a; and says the Boeotian in Ar.Ach.911,860, cf. Pl.Ep.345a

ἴτω.definition: 3sg. imper. from ; in Trag. almost an exclam., go to! S.Ph.120; well, well! E.Med.798

ἰύζω.definition: aor. Pi.P.4.237:—shout, yell, in order to scare beasts, Il.17.66; Od.15.162; later, yell from grief or pain, cry out, Pi. l.c.; used by A. in lyr., only in imper., Pers.281, cf. 1042, Supp.808, 872; part., S.Tr.787; C…

ἰχθυάω.definition: fish, angle, mostly in Ep. pres. and impf; sport , . . Hes.Sc.210

ἰχθυβόλος.definition: striking fish, catching fish; Subst., fisher, angler, ib.7.295 , 9.227

ἰχνεία.definition: casting about for the scent, of hounds, X.Cyn.3.7

ἰχνεύω.definition: track out, hunt after, S.Aj.20, OT221, 476; to hunt the mountains, X.Cyn.4.9

ἰδέ.definition: Ep. Conj., = and, Il.4.147, al; Cypr., then, in that case, Inscr.Cypr.135.12 H. and

ἱερωστί.definition: Ion. Adv. in holy sort, piously, Anacr.149

ἰμέσος.definition: Prep.,c.gen., between, Schwyzer664.17 ; also ib.25; prob. fr

ἰξυόθεν.definition: Adv. from the loins, Arat.144; prob. l. for in Opp.C.2.6

ἱππόθεν.definition: Adv., forth from the horse, of the heroes descending from the Trojan horse, Od.8.515, 11.531

ἰσαχῶς.definition: Adv., in the same number of ways, Arist.Metaph.1013a16, al.; ib.1054a14; in as many ways as, Id.EN1096a23

ἶφι.definition: Ep. Adv. by force or might, freq. in Hom., but only with four Verbs, Il.1.38, etc.; 1.151; 19.417, Od.18.156; Il.3.375; later Euph.90, etc.—Freq. in prop. names, e.g. etc

ἱλατήριον.definition: expiatory or propitiatory offering, Chron.Lind. B.49

ἰδιολογία.definition: subjective theorizing, dub. cj. in; private conversation, Charito4.6

ἰαμβέλεγος.definition: an asynartete verse, formed by substituting an iambic penthemimer for the former half of a pentameter, Heph.15.11

ἱππόνικος.definition: victorious in the chariot-race, Gloss., prob. l. in B.13.22: freq.as pr. n

ἰοβόρος.definition: poison-eating, Opp.C.3.223; of a; eating venomously, Nic.Th.467

ἰδιοφυής.definition: of peculiar nature, ib.1.7.20; D.S.5.30; title of work by Archelaus, D.L.2.17

ἴαμα.definition: Ion. remedy, medicine; = IG4.951.2 , cf. 1 Ep.Cor.12.9

ἵζημα.definition: subsidence, sinking, Str.1.3.17, cf. 2.3.6, Plu.2.434c : metaph., of language, Longin.9.13

ἱεροδόκος.definition: receiving sacrifices, or received in temples, A.Supp.363

ἰσχαλέος.definition: poet. for dried, Od.19.233; thin, paltry, Man.6.434:—later Eust.1863.60

ἴψ.definition: gen. nom. pl. :—wood-worm, Od.21.395, Thphr.HP8.10.5; found in vines, Id.CP3.22.5, Lap.49, Str.13.1.64

ἰσότονος.definition: pulling evenly, Gal.18.351; bearing the same accent, Hermog.Id.1.12

ἴλαρχος.definition: = I, IG4.487.2, al. ; = praefectus turmae, App.Hisp.43

ἰδιότοπος.definition: of their own district, cj. in Peripl.M.Rubr.47

ἰσοκωλία.definition: equality of members or clauses, Hermog.Id.1.12

ἰλλαίνω.definition: look awry, squint, of the eyes, to be distorted, Id.Coac.214, Epid.4.12:—so also in Pass., Id.Morb.3.12

ἰωχμός.definition: = through the rout, Il.8.89,158; Hes.Th.683, cf. Theoc.25.279

ἱπποτροφία.definition: breeding or keeping of horses, esp. for; as a liturgy, . . SIG1003.26

ἱλαρῶπις.definition: of gracious aspect, prob. in PMag.Lond.121.382

ἰξίας.definition: = chamaeleon-thistle, Cardopatium corymbiferum., Dsc.3.9, Alex.21, Gal.14.140

ἱπποπέδη.definition: horse-fetter, Hippiatr.106; a name given by Eudoxus to a figure-of-eight curve described by a planet, Simp.in Cael.497.3, Procl.in Euc.pp.127,128 F

ἰμπλατία.definition: Arc. for a sacrificial cake, IG5.4

ἰσοτριβής.definition: in A.Ag.1443, pressing the benches like others

ἰσοβαθής.definition: of equal depth, Thphr.CP3.4.2, Heliod. ap.Orib.46.8.2

ἱπποκομέω.definition: groom horses, groom his beetle, Ar.Pax74

ἰδιωτεύω.definition: occupy a private station, opp; practise privately, of a physician, opp. Pl.Plt.259a, cf. Grg.514e sq

ἱεροσκόπος.definition: inspecting victims; dub. l. in Cat.Cod.Astr.8.145

ἰουλίς.definition: rainbow-wrasse, Coris iulis, Arist.HA610b6, AP7.504.5 , Numen. ap. Ath.7.304f, Artem.1.14

ἰσχουρέω.definition: suffer from retention of urine, Aret.SD2.4, Herod.Med. ap.Orib.10.37.2

ἰλαδόν.definition: Adv., in troops, Il.2.93, Hdt.1.172 : generally, in abundance, Hes.Op.287

ἰατρεύω.definition: Ion. pf. Hp.Art.46: :—treat; abs., practise medicine, Hp.Art.72; Arist.Pol.1281b40

ἱερομνήμων.definition: representative sent by each Amphictyonic state to the Delphic Council, D.18.148, Jusj. ap. eund.24.150, IG22.1126.10, 1299.80, etc.; also at the Amphictyony of Calauria, ib.4.842

ἱερακίτης.definition: stone of the colour of a

ἱππόλοφος.definition: with horsehair crest, IG12.129 ; by comic metaph., Ar.Ra.818

ἰδίωμα.definition: peculiarity of style, D.H.Amm.2 tit., al; idiom, A.D.Synt.157.9

ἱππόφλομος.definition: giant i.e. belladonna, Atropa belladonna, Plin.HN25.148

ἰσχάς.definition: dried fig, Ar.Eq.755; spurge, Euphorbia Apios, Thphr.HP9.9.6, Dsc.4.175, Plin.HN26.72

ἱεράρχης.definition: president of sacred rites, high- priest, IG7.303 , 9.32 : Boeot. Schwyzer515.4,al.:—hence Boeot. to be high-priest, ib.544.4

ἰσαθάνατος.definition: equal to the Immortals, Arist.Fr.675.7 as quoted by Did.in D

ἰθύκυφος.definition: of parts of the normal spine, frontally concave, Hp.Art.45 ; opp. , frontally convex, ll. cc., cf. Gal.18.542

ἴς.definition: gen. acc. nom.pl. dat; later, the fibrous vessels in the muscles, Pl.Ti.84a, Arist.HA515b27, al.; in blood, fibrine, Id.PA650b14, cf. Pl.Ti.82c, MenoIatr.17.34: metaph., of metals, Plu.2.434b

ἱερόδρομος.definition: flowing in a sacred stream, Epigr.Gr.835b4 : poet. running in sacred races, Philox.15

ἱππιοχάρμης.definition: one who fights from a chariot; as Adj., the tumult of the horse-fight, ib.105; cf

ἱζηματίας.definition: earthquake which causes subsidence, Lyd.Ost.53; v.l. for in Arist.Mu.396a4

ἱεροποιός.definition: overseer of temples and sacred; as Adj., ib.80,9.40

ἰσόγαιος.definition: of equal height in relation to the land, Luc.Ner.5: Att. even with the ground, Thphr.CP3.7.3:—written IG22.1665

ἰσόψυχος.definition: of equal spirit, A.Ag.1470; of like soul or mind, Ep.Phil.2.20

ἰλλός.definition: squinting , to get a squint, Ar.Th.846: Comp. Sophr.158, cf. Gal.17.680

ἰσοελκής.definition: equal in weight, Nic.Th.41, v.l. ib.44

ἰσώνυμος.definition: bearing the same name as, c. gen., Pi.O.9.64; i.e. Nic.Th.678

ἰσόπαις.definition: like a child, as of a child, A.Ag.75

ἱκανοδότης.definition: one who gives security, BGU1189.3; one who requites, PMasp.6ii82

ἱεράκιον.definition: hawk-weed: = Urospermum; a compound eyesalve, Gal.12.783

ἰχνοπέδη.definition: a kind of fetter or trap, AP6.109 , 7.626

ἰσοδίαιτος.definition: living on an equal footing, with one, Th.1.6; Luc.Bis Acc.33

ἱεροθυτέω.definition: sacrifice, Heraclit.Incred.39, cf. IG14.290 , 12.67 : Arc. pres. part. nom. sg. masc. ib.5.3.7

ἰθυσκόλιος.definition: curved in one direction, though straight in another, of the normal spine, Hp.Art.45

ἰπνευτής.definition: = furnarius, Gloss.; prob. for in AP6.299

ἱρωσύνη.definition: Ion. for priesthood, v.l. in Hdt.4.161

ἴσθμιος.definition: also E.Tr.1098 :—of or belonging to the Isthmus, Isthmian, Pi.O.13.4; S.OT940

ἱκεσία.definition: = Plu.Them.24. but metri gr. in AP l.c., Procl.H.1.36.]

ἱππομανής.definition: abounding in, swarming with horses; as Subst., an Arcadian plant, thorn-apple, Datura stramonium, of which horses are madly fond, or which makes them mad, Theoc.2.48; f.l. for in Thphr.HP9.15.6

ἰδιωτεία.definition: private station, opp; uncouthness, want of education, Luc.Hist.Conscr.27, Abd.7

ἰδιωτίζω.definition: pronounce in the local manner, Eust.145.10

ἰώ.definition: an exclam., chiefly in dramatic poetry; freq. also of grief or suffering, oh! S.Ant.850; Id.OC199, etc.; AP7.468 ; ib.434 : c. gen., . . A.Ag.1305; E.Ph.1290; Ar.Ach.1205

ἰσολύμπιος.definition: like those rendered to the Olympians; ranking with the Olympic games, SIG630.13 , cf. IG12.506.7 , etc

ἰουλόπεζος.definition: footed like the centipede, i.e. many-footed, many-oared, of a ship, Lyc.23

ἰατρεία.definition: Ion. healing, medical; metaph., curing, correcting, Arist.Pol.1267a7; ib.1272b2, cf.1284b19, Plu.2.510c; Arist.EN1152b32: pl., ib.1104b17, al

ἰτέϊνος.definition: of willow, Hdt.4.67; made of withy rods, wicker, Theoc.16.79

ἰσότιμος.definition: equal in honour or privilege; generally, equal in value: hence, equal, Ph.2.248; Hdn.2.3.6; evenly balanced, Ael.NA10.1

ἰδιογενής.definition: mating only with its kind, opp; peculiar in kind, Herm. ap.Stob.1.49.44, Dsc.2.66

ἱπποσείρης.definition: one who leads a horse by the rein, Anacr.75.6

ἰλύς.definition: dregs, sediment, Id.Mul.1.66; of wine, Arist.GA753a24, al; impurity, Gal.1.603, cf. 616; Androm. ap. eund.14.35. Choerob.in Theod.1.331; gen. APl.4.230 , A.R.1.10, but Il. l.c.]

ἰνάριον.definition: Dim. of strand, fibre, Phlp.in Mete.61.31

ἱπποπόλος.definition: herding horses, of the Thracians, Il.13.4, 14.227

ἰθυμαχία.definition: Ion. fair, stand-up fight, Hdt.4.120; ib.102

ἰάτρευμα.definition: = Dam.Isid.189 : Rhet. in pl., 'specifics' for allaying prejudice, etc., Arist.Rh.1415a25

ἰσομοιρία.definition: Ion. equal share; equability, of climate, Hp.Aër.12; Gal.1.534

ἱπποκόρυθος.definition: coined as compd. of and Porph.adIl.2.1

ἰοδνεφής.definition: dark as the flower , purple-dark, Od.4.135,9.426

ἱερακίδιον.definition: statuette of a hawk, Roussel Cultes Égyptiens 219

ἰσήλικος.definition: equal in magnitude, Ph.Bel.91.21; equal in age, Procl.in Prm.p.944S., al., Dam.Pr.316

ἱππασία.definition: riding, horse-exercise, Ar.Ach.1165; chariot-driving, Luc.DDeor.12.1, etc

ἰσωνυμία.definition: rejected as a name for a pronoun by A.D.Pron.9.7

ἰσόχοος.definition: of the same number of Hp.Morb.2.26

ἰσῆλιξ.definition: of the same age with, X.Smp.8.1, Com.Adesp.874: c. gen., Ph.1.6: abs., Id.2.303

ἱπποβότης.definition: feeder of horses; at Chalcis in Euboea a social class , Knights, Hdt.5.77, 6.100; Arist.Fr.603

ἱμερόφρων.definition: lovely in spirit, Doroth. ap. Heph.Astr.3.9

ἰξευτής.definition: fowler, bird-catcher, Lyc.105; as Adj., catching with birdlime, AP6.152

ἰπόω.definition: press, squeeze, Cratin.91; esp. in surgery, Hp.Art.47; Heliod. ap. Orib.49.13.8:—Pass., to be weighed down, A.Pr.365; Ar.Eq.924

ἰχώρ.definition: ichor, the juice, not blood, that; the watery part of animal juices, serum , of the blood, Hp.Cord.11, Pl.Ti.83c, Arist.HA521b2 , PA651a18; of gall, Hp.Acut.1; of milk, whey, Arist.HA521b27; gravy of underdone meat, A…

ἰσόψηφος.definition: with or by an equal number of votes; having an equal vote with others, Th.1.141, cf. 3.11; of a commander, ib.79; Pl.Lg.692a; of communities, possessing an equal franchise, E.Supp.353

ἱερόχθων.definition: poet. gen. of hallowed soil, IG14.1389ii27

ἴονθος.definition: root of a hair, young hair; eruption on the face, which often accompanies the first growth of the beard, etc., Arist.HA556b29, Pr.963b40, Erot. s.v. :—hence Thphr.Sud.16, cf. Gal.12.824

ἰσότεχνος.definition: equal in art or skill, Epigr.Gr.532 ; Plu.Nob.9

ἰσόπεδος.definition: of even surface, level; c. dat., level or even with, Hdt.4.201, cf. D.S.19.94, Plu.Num.10

ἰδιοτρόφος.definition: feeding individuals, Pl.Plt.261d; feeding on a peculiar diet, opp. Arist.HA488a15

ἰσόκοιλος.definition: with equal cavities, Plu.2.1021a, Theo Sm.p.60 H

ἰσοσκέλεια.definition: having two sides equal; in trine aspect, Ptol.Tetr.125

ἰσχνότης.definition: thinness, leanness; of style, spareness, i.e. plainness, of Lysias, D.H.Vett.Cens.5.1; cf. Phld.Rh.1.165S., Demetr.Eloc.14

ἰδιοπαθέω.definition: suffer from a local affection, Gal.8.31

ἰσάμιλλος.definition: equal in the race: neut. pl. as Adv., AP9.311

ἰδιοθρονέω.definition: Astrol., of a planet, enjoy its proper dignity, Ptol.Tetr.51, Paul.Al.S.4

ἱστότονος.definition: stretched on the loom, v.l. in the codd. other than Rav. for Ar.Ra.1315; E.Hyps.Fr.1 ii 10

ἱερόσυλος.definition: temple-robber, or; of things, got by sacrilege, Eub.7.4

ἰξοβόλος.definition: setting limed twigs: as Subst., fowler, Man.4.243

ἰσοψηφία.definition: equality of votes, D.H.7.64; equal right to vote, Plu.CG9

ἰσοπραξία.definition: a faring equally, like condition, Eust.662.35

ἱερουλίζω.definition: of wine, dub. sens. in Alex.Trall.10

ἰκμαίνω.definition: moisten, Nic.Al.112:— Med., anoint one's body, A.R.3.847:—Pass., to be wetted, to be wet, Nic.Fr.70.8, A.R.4.1066

ἰσάξιος.definition: of equal worth, Porph.Abst.2.55; Procl.in Cra.p.50 P.; Iamb.Myst.3.21; adequate, Dam.Pr.43, cf. 28. Adv. Iamb.Myst.9.7

ἵππευμα.definition: ride on horseback or journey in a chariot, E.IT1428; Id.Fr.114

ἱπποβάμων.definition: trotting like a horse, or used for riding, A.Supp.284; metaph., high-paced words, bombast, fustian, Ar.Ra.821

ἱλαρόω.definition: gladden, brighten, LXXSi.7.24,al., Aristeas108; Phld.Mus.p.99 K.:—also LXXPs.103.15:—Pass., fut. aor. PMag.Leid.W.12.30, 5.20

ἱππεύω.definition: to be a horseman or rider, ride, Hdt.1.136; metaph., of the wind, E.Ph.212 ; Id.Supp.994 ; also, rush, Id.HF1001

ἱπποφοβάς.definition: horse-fear, a fabulous plant, Ps.-Democr. ap. Plin.HN24.161

ἱπποτυφία.definition: horse-pride, i.e. excessive pride or conceit, Luc.Hist.Conscr.45, Pl. ap. D.L.3.39

ἴκταρ.definition: Adv. close together, thickly (=; Prep. c. gen., close to, hard by, A.Ag.116 ; Id.Eu.998 : c. dat., Alcm.23.80: abs., . . do not strike even near him, are quite wide of the mark, prov. in Pl.R.575c, cf. Ael.NA15.29

ἵλαμαι.definition: = h.Hom.19.48, 21.5; Orph.A.944; cf. in h.Hom., in Orph.]

ἰσόρροπος.definition: in equipoise, of the balance; generally, well-balanced, well-matched, of a man with his legs of the same length, Hp.Fract.19; of a nose, flattened, but not awry, Id.Art.37; of a bone, cylindrical, ib.34; opp. ib.50; e…

ἰοβολέω.definition: shoot arrows, dart, A.R.4.1440, AP5.187; emit poison, Gp.2.47.12

ἴφυον.definition: spike-lavender, Lavandula Spica, Ar.Th.910 , Fr.560 , Epich.161, Thphr.HP6.6.11, 6.8.3

ἱππολεχής.definition: having given birth to a horse, Orac. ap. Paus.8.42.6

ἰσόογκος.definition: of equal bulk or volume, Simp.in Cael.691.35, in Ph.1016.23

ἰπνός.definition: oven, furnace, Hp.Morb.2.47; the place of the oven, i.e. the kitchen, Semon.7.61, Ar.V.837, Lycurg.Fr.73

ἰθύφαλλος.definition: fascinum erectum, the phallos carried in; ode and dance performed at such festivals, Hyp.Fr.50, Duris13J

ἰσόδομος.definition: of walls, built in equal courses, Vitr.2.8.6, Plin.HN36.171

ἰασπίζω.definition: to be like a jasper, Dsc.5.136

ἰσεννύω.definition: to be of an intermediate age, Hp.Mul.2.111 )

ἰσομερής.definition: equally divided, BGU1122.12 ; of equal length, ib.393.12 : generally, equal, Just.Nov.97.1

ἱππεία.definition: riding or driving of horses; cavalry, X.An.5.6.8,Ages.1.23

ἱππόλυτος.definition: letting horses loose, dub. l. in APl.4.44

ἱππομιγής.definition: partly a horse, half-horse half-man, Ael.VH9.16

ἰυγή.definition: = howling, shrieking, as of men in pain, Orac. ap. Hdt.9.43, S.Ph.752;= AB267; but also of the shout of heralds, Tim.Pers.233; the hissing of snakes, Nic.Th.400, Opp.H.1.565. Orac. ap. Hdt. l.c., Nic.; in S.l.c.]

ἱερόπολις.definition: holy city, Ph.2.146; of the cities of refuge, ib.308, 321

ἰαχέω.definition: aor. 1 h.Cer.20, AP7.745 (Antip; rarely c. acc. obj., bewail, E.Ph.1295, cf. [1523]:—Pass., . . thou wert proclaimed . . , Id.Hel.1147

ἱππηδόν.definition: Adv. like a horse, A.Th.328 , Supp.431; like a horseman, Ar.Pax81

ἱστοπέδη.definition: Dor. a piece of wood set in the keel to which the mast was bound, or, a hole in the keel for stepping the mast, Od.12.51,162, Alc.18.6

ἰδιοβουλέω.definition: follow one's own counsel, take one's own way, , D.C.43.27

ἱδρωτοειδῶς.definition: Adv. after the manner of sweat, Steph.in Hp.1.112 D

ἰδιοπάθεια.definition: Medic., affection having a local origin, Gal.8.31, al., Alex.Aphr.Pr.2.35

ἱππαστής.definition: as Adj., fit for riding, of a horse, X.Eq.10.17

ἴκτερος.definition: jaundice, Hp.Aph.4.62 , Morb.2.38; a bird of a yellowish-green colour, by looking at which a jaundiced person was cured—the bird died! Plin.HN30.94

ἶδος.definition: sweat: pl., sweats, Hp.Coac.105; warmth, Emp.62.5, prob. in Id.21.4; violent heat, Hes.Sc.397, Call.Fr.124 , D.P.966; cf

ἱερόστολος.definition: an Egyptian priest who had charge of the sacred vestments, = Plu.2.352b

ἰξία.definition: = I, Thphr.HP3.16.1, CP2.17.1, prob. in; = pine-thistle, Atractylis gummifera, Dsc.3.8, Plin. HN22.45; Thphr.HP9.1.3

ἱερακίζω.definition: behave like a hawk, Thphr.Sign.16, Arist.Fr.253

ἰσοπολίτης.definition: enjoying equal political rights; enjoying reciprocity of rights, of the citizens of Roman municipia, D.H.8.76:—fem. of cities enjoying such rights, = municipia, App.BC1.10

ἱστιόκωπος.definition: with oars and sails, a type of boat, Gell. 10.25.5

ἴχνευσις.definition: tracking, X.Cyn.3.4, 10.5; method of investigation, cj. in Epicur.Ep.2p.42U

ἰσόδενδρος.definition: equal to that of a tree; as big as a tree, Thphr.HP3.1.1

ἱππελάτης.definition: driver or rider of horses, Opp.C.1.95

ἰαμβιστής.definition: one who writes iambics, libeller, Ath.5.181c

ἰδιωτισμός.definition: way or fashion of a common person; Rhet., argumentum ad hominem, usu. in the form of a hypothetical question, Rufin.Fig.10

ἰδιόγραφος.definition: written with one's own hand; specially or separately written, LXXPs.151 tit

ἱδρώς.definition: and Aeol. Sapph.2.13; exudation of trees, gum, resin, E.Ion1175; Ion Trag.40; of wine, Antiph.52.12

ἴλλοψ.definition: coined as etym. of Ath.7.308b,c, cf. Plu.2.728e

ἰβηρίς.definition: pepperwort, Lepidium graminifolium, Damocr. ap.Gal.13.350; = Aët.ap. Ps.-Dsc.2.174

ἰασιώνη.definition: bindweed, Convolvulus sepium, Thphr.HP1.13.2, cf. Plin.HN21.105

ἰθυωρίη.definition: Ion. for direction, straightness, of a limb, etc., Hp.Off.15 , Fract.30, al

ἴσως.definition: Lacon. , Adv. of equally, in; equally, with reference to equality, Arist.Pol.1283b40; fairly, equitably, Aen. Tact.22.24; D.10.74; D.H.10.40; Plb.23.2.7

ἰσχομένως.definition: Adv., with checks or hindrances, Pl.Cra.415c

ἰσοτέλεστος.definition: made exactly like, exact; coming at the last to all alike, of Death, S.OC1220
